content:
incident-bot: PAGER — P1: Private Gateway connectivity degraded in azure-centralus. Multiple Private deployments reporting TCP resets and failed handshakes. Auto-detect flagged at 02:07 UTC. Pager: @akash-sre

incident-bot: Affected services: private-tenant-vpn, private-replay, private-ingress. Initial anomaly rate: 18% 5xx on private routes. Link: https://internal.ops/incident/1789204821

akash-sre: ack — I'm on it. Pulling control-plane logs and BGP sessions. Starting with peering table and metrics from our edge routers.

maria-net: seeing BGP flaps on our Azure ExpressRoute peers. Example syslog: ```Apr 12 02:08:33 bgpd[4142]: neighbor 198.51.100.2 DOWN: hold timer expired```

josh-sre: I can reproduce TCP RSTs from a few customer tunnels. traceroute path shows transit dropping after Azure hop 4:
```traceroute to 10.11.12.1 (10.11.12.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1 10.0.0.1 0.3 ms 0.2 ms 0.2 ms
 2 198.51.100.10 1.1 ms 1.0 ms 1.0 ms
 3 198.51.100.2 5.6 ms 5.7 ms 5.6 ms
 4 * * *
```

maria-net: confirmed — Azure reported packet-loss spikes on vWAN in centralus. Their status page shows intermittent routing updates but no public incident yet. We have an open ticket with MSFT (case 987654321).

akash-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new private sessions to fallback region (azure-eastus2 / gcp-us-central1) where Private Relay/peers are healthy, 2) enable short-term prefix failover in control plane for affected customers, 3) notify customers and schedule maintenance windows for longer-term BGP stability.

lia-oncall: I'm ready to take over traffic steering. @deploy-bot can you push failover policy patch to control plane? Keep it canary to 10% initially.

deploy-bot: rolling config change: `canary_failover=10% -> target_regions=[azure-eastus2,gcp-us-central1]` to route-service v4. ETA 30s.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for canary. Observing per-tenant telemetry: 8 tenants shifted, error rates for those tenants decreased from 22% -> 2% in 3m.

erin-support: prepping customer comms. Draft: "We've detected intermittent networking instability in Azure Central US affecting Private Gateway connectivity. We're rerouting traffic to fallbacks and monitoring. Root cause under investigation with Microsoft." Want approval to send to impacted accounts.

akash-sre: approve. Add note: include support case number and recommended temporary steps for customer-side: ensure BGP timers are default, avoid long-lived sessions until routing stable.

cloud-contacts: Microsoft support response: "We see an internal route flap in CentralUS vWAN fabric; mitigation underway. Estimated stabilization 30-45 minutes. Case 987654321 updated."

maria-net: pushing additional BGP hold-time increase on our side to tolerate transient flaps: `neighbor X timers 180 540` for affected peers. Monitoring for side-effects.

josh-sre: monitoring AGG metrics — overall private-traffic latency improved 14% after canary failover. No increased error rates on fallback regions.

akash-sre: decision: expand failover from 10% -> 60% for affected ASN blocks to reduce customer impact while MSFT stabilizes. Lia, you lead the rollout. Josh, watch for cross-region latency spikes.

lia-oncall: starting expansion now — will progress in 10% increments with 2m observation windows.

lia-oncall: 20% -> stable. 30% -> stable. 40% -> one tenant saw IPC timeouts, rollback 40% -> 30% and investigating.

josh-sre: IPC timeout correlated to an aggressive idle-timeout on the tenant's VPN appliance. Support notified that tenant to adjust idle timers; we've rolled back that tenant to centralus to avoid disruption.

lia-oncall: continuing rollout. 50% -> stable. 60% -> stable. Current coverage: ~320 other tenants now served from fallback regions. Error rate cluster-wide down to 3%.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Microsoft reports fabric control-plane stabilization. PR gratuits: patch applied at 02:40 UTC. Monitoring.

akash-sre: okay, maintain failover for another 45 minutes while we validate BGP session stability. If Azure confirms stable BGP for 30m, we'll start returning traffic.

erin-support: customer update sent at 02:46 UTC. Received a handful of replies — two customers asked for longer-term remediation timeline; escalated to account teams.

cloud-contacts: MSFT confirms no further flapping for 40m and BGP sessions are stable. They will keep the internal mitigation active for 2h before full fabric normalization.

akash-sre: begin controlled reintroduction back to centralus in 15m windows, 20% increments. Lia, coordinate and watch for anomalies.

lia-oncall: reintroduction started. 20% -> stable. 40% -> stable. 60% -> two tenants show increased latency; we paused and notified account teams.

josh-sre: dig on the two tenants — looks like their appliances had not re-synced routes post-failover. Assisted with route refresh (`clear ip bgp *` equivalents on customer side) and pushed soft-reconfig on our control-plane.

lia-oncall: resumed reintroduction. 80% -> stable. 100% -> stable. All private routes returned to centralus by 03:55 UTC.

akash-sre: declaring incident recovered at 03:58 UTC. Post-incident action items: 1) run a DR drill for cross-region failover for Private Gateway, 2) bake automated route-refresh step when returning from failover, 3) review BGP timer defaults for partners. I'll create the postmortem doc.

erin-support: sending final customer note and survey.

oncall-scheduler: next oncall handoff: @lia-oncall takes primary for follow-up postmortem work; @akash-sre will stay on the incident/P1 follow-through for 4h.

akash-sre: handing off to Lia for write-up. Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. :thumbsup:

lia-oncall: acknowledged. I'll kick off the postmortem draft and action items in #postmortems. Closing thread for paging; keep this thread for follow-ups only.
